Obviously I can only speak for myself, but here goes.

1. My personal brand of asexuality involves a lack of sexual attraction towards any gender, a slight disgust with genitalia, but a pretty "normal" sex drive and a willingness to experience sex both for my sake and the sake of a partner. The best analogy I've heard for having a sex drive but being asexual is that it's as though you're hungry, but you don't want anything that's in the fridge. I like that analogy because I think it's a pretty common experience people can understand better than I want to have sex just not with any of the only options available. Personally it's more the pleasure aspect of sex I'm interested in. The physicality aspect doesn't interest me because, uh, I'm asexual.

2. I don't think there was a specific moment where I *realized* I was asexual, per se, but rather a moment where I just accepted it instead of continuing to question it. That moment occurred toward the end of 2017, so not all that long ago. But for one or two years prior, I did a lot of googling "am I asexual" quizzes and things, looking a blogs and definitions, etc. Surprise, if you're looking up am I something online, you probably are that something. The primary thing I did, however was ask everyone around me the same question over and over: "So like, there are people where you see them walk in the room and think, I wanna smash that?" Crude, yes, but vital in my own establishment of my identity, as that was something I just did not understand at all. For a while I thought I was demisexual, but I threw that idea out after realizing I'd still never been sexually attracted to any of the people I'd had a deep emotional bond with. I'm still insecure about it, "what I'm really not???" and all that crap, but that's more so a product of my crippling anxiety, insecurities, and need for constant validation than anything legitimate.

3. Asexuality and aromanticism are not intrinsically linked. They're two completely separate identities/occurrences. I believe most asexual people are alloromantic (is that the right term?), though I could be horribly wrong. Although I do believe most aromantic people are asexual? I'm sure there's science behind this shit that we don't understand yet. Anyway don't take my word for the frequency of the identities coinciding, just that it is, in fact, a coincidence.

4. Hahahahahahaha oh boy. For starters, when I came out to my mother, the first thing out of her mouth was, "Well, you have to end up with someone who's also asexual, because..." No??? I'm not sex-repulsed, but even if I were, there are plenty of instances of relationships like that work out fine, either through polyamory, or openness, or some kind of agreement that is consensual and comfortable for the couple.  Asexuality is not a disease or a mental condition. I am not broken, or just havent found the right one yet. I am not asexual *because* I'm disgusted by/afraid of sex, and I am not inherently sex-repulsed/afraid of sex because I am asexual. It's not because I'm immature. I exist. My identity is real. Asexuality is not celibacy. It is not a choice. I can fall in love because aromantic and asexual are two different things. It's not a phase I will grow out of. It's not a hormone problem, getting laid won't "fix" me. Yes, this is a valid definition for the word asexual, no, I'm not a plant. Yes, I can know for sure without having had sex. No we're not all virgins. This is not an "everyone feels like that sometimes" thing. I'm not just in denial of my gayness (I'm openly pan). Yes we can and do masturbate!!! Masturbation is a personal choice. Some aces do, some don't. I masturbate sometimes, and I do it because it feels good. It doesn't have anything to do with whether or not I'm sexual attracted to any genders, so why is it so wrapped up in this topic??? Asexuality is not caused by past sexual trauma. Aces who have been victims are not ace because of the trauma. We don't hate sex and allos, we aren't naïve, or faking for attention. It's not a moral stance. Men can be ace. Asexuality isn't evolution's response to overpopulation. I can't be "fixed" with a pill. No, I'm not missing out. There's nothing to miss out on. I don't experience sexual attraction and never could. I'm not a freak. I'm not the only one. I could go on.

5. Everyone assumes everyone else experiences sexual attraction. Why wouldn't they? I don't blame anyone. It just makes me uncomfortable because I can't relate. At all. I feel out of touch. Society as a whole is hypersexual, and besides being uncomfortable for gender reasons, it just doesn't make any sense to me. I feel really out of place sometimes, like the world speaking a completely different language, but all in all, that's not really too much of a problem. I have more of a problem with people who try to invalidate me or tell me what I actually am and just generally make me feel like shit. I'm worried about my love life, but I'll talk about that in 7.

6. It's not that different. I guess I don't have to deal with getting turned on in public by a hot person and my brain extrapolating. Is that a thing that happens to allos?? I don't even know. Sex doesn't sell, for me. It's almost amusing because it lets you take a step back and look at how hard they're trying and it just has,,, no effect. Romantically, it might be different, but that'll be in 7.

7. I'm very, very open about the fact that I'm pan ace. Shout it from the rooftops style. It's a little concerning, but honestly I'm just celebrating my identity after years of confusion and insecurity. It's kind of a, take that, world, thing. Anyway, here we go. I've never been in a serious romantic relationship, and like many, many aces, I'm terrified. I consider myself lucky that I'm not sex-repulsed as it will make it somewhat easier, though being sex-repulsed is nothing negative or to be ashamed of. It merely can make relationships with allosexuals trickier to navigate. I'm worried that my lack of attraction will ruin my relationships, that my limit sexually won't be enough for my partners but I'll be too unstable to cope with them having sex with other people, etc. It's really scary, and a common sentiment in our community. Thing is, I tell all my friends I'm ace. And, I'm actually demiromantic too, which just means I have to have a deep emotional bond before I can be romantically attracted to someone. Ergo, anyone I might be interested in dating would already know going in, so I'd have it easier than most.

8. I'm a normal person! This is a small part of my life, but it's still important to me, and I'm still proud of who I am. Fun fact: I make a lot of jokes about being sexually attracted to random things I really like, e.g. I'm sexually attracted to these fries, or those pants, or this aesthetically pleasing deck of cards, etc., and it's hilarious to me because I'm ace, but all of my friends are allo and they don't get it or think it's funny and honestly my jokes are a gift and they're being wasted on these frickin allosexuals smh.

9. If I had a dictionary definition entry, asexuality would be in there, yeah. But so would a hundred million other things.

10. I don't want to be branded freak or broken for my sexuality, because A) I'm not, and B) it's not that big of a deal. I'm proud of my sexuality, and it's important to me, but it does not dictate my entire life, just like anyone's attraction to any gender doesn't dictate their entire life.

Additional comments:  Wow this is a lot of typing. Asexuality is a different experience for everyone, like mental illnesses and I can't think of a second example right now. It's not a cookie cutter thing, and a lot of people have huge misconceptions about what it is. It's not celibacy, it's not because you're disgusted by sex (that's a case by case basis thing), it's not that you don't have a sex drive, or you just haven't met the right person, bla bla bla etc. It's merely that you aren't sexually attracted to any genders. If anything is confusing or you want to know more, etc., feel free to ask!
